dedupe_keys.name: item open data and harmonized transport database

description: The iTEM Open Database is a harmonised transport dataset of historical values from 1970 to the present, assembled by the International Transport Energy Modeling (iTEM) consortium from publicly available sources. Each source dataset is downloaded, cleaned and harmonised to common region and technology definitions, and a rule book documents for every dataset its name, the link to the original source, the link to the Python cleaning script, the variables and the cleaning steps in plain English. The Zenodo deposit holds the harmonised CSV (about 11 MB) and the rule book PDF, with authors including Humberto Linero, Sonia Yeh, Paul Kishimoto, Pierpaolo Cazzola, Lewis Fulton, David McCollum, Joshua Miller, Page Kyle and Manuel Pérez Bravo; the code is on GitHub under the transportenergy organisation. Coverage is global by region. Access: free download under CC BY 4.0 (version dated 11 September 2024). Caveats: values inherit the gaps of the public sources, and the harmonised regions may not match national boundaries. It supports calibration of transport energy and demand models, long-run scenario and capacity planning studies and cross-checks between statistics sources, and complements the ITF transport statistics and the SSP transport demand dataset catalogued here.
